generated_examples.rule: Each source row becomes one research-only example with the same official URL, fact, gate and confidence. No parcel relation or legal/planning conclusion is inferred.

second_pass_examples.rule: Each source row is rendered a second time as a fail-closed control. The same source fact is retained and the gate is prefixed 'Second-pass control'. This checks that dataset presence, designation or legal instrument is not silently promoted to parcel-level outcome.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data says listed-building outlines are incomplete and do not consistently represent curtilage.
extra_examples.gate: Do not use outline intersection alone as definitive listed-building curtilage.

extra_examples.fact: Standing advice notes some ancient woodland, including smaller sites, may be absent from inventories.
extra_examples.gate: No inventory hit must not be converted into no ancient-woodland risk.

extra_examples.fact: Natural England consent for SSSI operations does not replace other permissions.
extra_examples.gate: Keep SSSI consent, planning permission and other licences as separate legal states.

extra_examples.fact: Scheduled monument consent is a separate regime for works affecting scheduled monuments.
extra_examples.gate: Planning permission must not be treated as scheduled monument consent.

extra_examples.ref: TPO legal instrument versus protected geometry
extra_examples.fact: TPO legal instrument records and protected tree/zone geography are modelled separately.
extra_examples.gate: Apply a TPO parcel constraint only after exact live order-to-tree/zone-to-parcel relation is verified.

extra_examples.ref: World Heritage designation versus statutory controls
extra_examples.fact: World Heritage status is protected through the planning system and related designations rather than creating a standalone extra statutory consent regime.
extra_examples.gate: Assess exact Outstanding Universal Value, setting and related designations for the proposal.
